android_mechanism: The complete SAX character buffer is copied on every text event; fix avoids the per-event copy
bug_description: FeedParser.extractTag locates the closing tag with xml.toLowerCase().indexOf(...), materializing a full lowercase copy of the item fragment for every extracted tag. Parsing one RSS item extracts ~6 tags (title/link/description/date/guid/author), so each refresh of a feed with N items allocates and scans ~6N full-fragment lowercase copies on the parsing thread, increasing GC pressure and feed-refresh latency.
fix_summary: The closing tag is located with a case-insensitive regex over the remaining substring, eliminating the per-tag lowercase copy while preserving case-insensitive matching semantics.
trigger_steps: Add several large RSS/Atom feeds (or one feed with 100+ long articles) to the reader.
Start hitrace capture (categories: app, sched, memory).
Trigger 刷新全部 (refresh all feeds).
Stop hitrace after refresh completes. Repeat 3 repetitions for unfixed, then install the fixed HAP and repeat 3 repetitions.

test_oracle.definition: CPU time of the feed parsing phase per refresh (from first article parse to last, before DB insert), plus count/size of large short-lived string allocations (GC events in memory trace).
test_oracle.comparison: unfixed performs one full-fragment toLowerCase copy per extracted tag (~6 per item); fixed none. unfixed parse CPU and GC activity > fixed by >= 15% on feeds with long descriptions.

trace_config.command: hdc shell hitrace --time 40 app sched memory -o /data/local/tmp/sr_parse.chtrace
